strategy.summary: Build pandas at the buggy commit ada009a40356 from source and run the PR's parametrized tslibs test test_to_datetime_barely_inside_bounds. On the buggy revision the two sub-microsecond timestamps (.145224193 and .145224999) should raise OverflowError inside array_to_datetime, so those cases fail; the .145225000 case should pass on both revisions. On the fixed revision all three should pass. Environment versions are not documented, so NumPy and the other packages are chosen by me and labelled as such.

pinned_because: numpy<2: no documented constraint and no era table entry for NumPy; this is my inferred choice for a pandas 2.2-era dev tree, not a documented requirement, so it is era-inferred and unverified
cython: documented in README without a version constraint; installed unpinned as the README's build step requires it
pyarrow: deliberately not installed; the 14.0.2 version comes from issue #57150's reporting environment, is not a documented requirement, and is not needed for this tslibs test

strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision ada009a40356 the test FAILS for the two sub-microsecond parameters (.145224193 and .145224999), because tslib.array_to_datetime raises OverflowError before the assertion is reached; the .145225000 parameter passes there. On the fixed revision (the PR's commit) all three parameters PASS, because array_to_datetime returns an M8[ns] array exactly equal to np.array(..., dtype='M8[ns]') under tm.assert_numpy_array_equal.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import pandas as pd; print(pd.Timestamp('1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224193').value)"  (fixed revision should print -9223372036854775807; buggy revision should raise OverflowError)
risks: The buggy path is only hit when microseconds equals min_nanoseconds/1000 - 1 and the sub-microsecond part is in the stated range; the PR's test values satisfy this, but a different sample would not transition.

The overflow is signed int64 arithmetic in C. Without sanitizers the buggy build may wrap rather than raise on some compilers or optimisation levels; the OverflowError in the issue shows the explicit range check fires in the reported build, but a different compiler or -O level could change which symptom appears. The transition is still expected to be a failure on the buggy revision.
The exact overflow site is not settled in the evidence; the discussion questions whether the scaling helpers themselves should change. This matters only for diagnosis, not for the transition.

Platform: the 64-bit int64 range assumed here holds on 64-bit builds. Behaviour is not evidenced on 32-bit or non-x86 platforms, and no architecture-specific failure is recorded, so the strategy assumes a standard 64-bit Linux x86_64 build.
NumPy version is not documented. A NumPy 2.x build may fail to compile or may change datetime handling in ways not evidenced here; numpy<2 is my chosen, era-inferred pin.
Editable build with --no-build-isolation requires Cython and a C compiler present in the environment before the build step; the build is slow, and a missing toolchain would fail before any test runs.
No sanitiser or special threading setting is evidenced as necessary, so none is planned.

oracle.reference_source: np.array(..., dtype='M8[ns]') in the test itself
oracle.why: The test compares int64 nanosecond values for exact equality via tm.assert_numpy_array_equal; no numeric tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On ada009a40356 array_to_datetime raises OverflowError from scaleMicrosecondsToNanoseconds for the .145224193 and .145224999 inputs, so the test errors before the assertion is reached.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the PR's fixed commit all three parametrized inputs convert to the expected M8[ns] values and the exact array equality assertion holds.
